title: Plain-Text Cognitive Architecture for Claude Code (HN Show HN — marciopuga/cog)
description: HN 'Show HN' by marciopuga presenting 'Cog' — a three-tier plain-text memory architecture for Claude Code: Hot (always-loaded, <50 lines), Warm (contextually loaded domain files), Glacier (archived YAML-frontmatter files). Includes a progressive retrieval protocol (L0: one-line relevance comments → L1: header scan → L2: full read), a Zettelkasten-inspired Thread synthesis system, and slash commands (/reflect, /evolve, /foresight, /housekeeping). Explicitly credits: Zep/Graphiti, Mem0, Zettelkasten, Basic Memory, Claude Memory as prior art.
redundancy_status: OVERLAPPING — substantial prior art acknowledged by author; mostly incremental over existing MEMORY.md + CLAUDE.md hierarchy
redundancy_comparison: Existing system: file-based MEMORY.md index + typed .md files (user/feedback/project/reference) with frontmatter, organized by domain. Cog's hot/warm/glacier tiers map onto existing global/project/local CLAUDE.md hierarchy. The Q&A memory framing described in the discovery was misattributed — it's a commenter's insight (user Real_Egor), not the project's design. The /foresight cross-domain synthesis command and L0/L1/L2 retrieval protocol are the most novel elements, both unproven.

community_metrics.community_sentiment: Mixed — several skeptics invoked XKCD #927 (standards proliferation); substantive debate about whether it solves a real problem over structured CLAUDE.md

key_findings: The Q&A memory framing in the discovery was a commenter's elaboration (user Real_Egor), NOT the project's architecture
The project explicitly credits Zep/Graphiti, Mem0, Zettelkasten, Basic Memory as prior art — author acknowledges this is synthesis
No empirical evidence for hallucination reduction — no benchmarks, no ablation studies
The /foresight command (cross-domain strategic synthesis) is the author's claimed differentiator; unproven
L0/L1/L2 retrieval protocol is a practical pattern but incremental over existing context management techniques
Three-tier hot/warm/glacier maps closely to existing global/project/local CLAUDE.md hierarchy
Community skeptical: XKCD 927 reference indicates perceived redundancy

evaluation.reasoning: The core novelty claim (Q&A-directed memory) was misattributed in the discovery — it belongs to a commenter, not the project. The actual Cog architecture is a well-structured synthesis of prior art that the author explicitly acknowledges (Zettelkasten, Mem0, Graphiti, Basic Memory). Three-tier storage, SSOT, and append-only observation logs all have prior art with no demonstrated advantage over the existing MEMORY.md + CLAUDE.md hierarchy. The /foresight synthesis command is the most plausible novel element but has zero empirical support. Community validation is modest (152 HN upvotes, 260 stars, mixed reception). Token efficiency may be neutral-to-negative: adding L0/L1/L2 retrieval overhead doesn't clearly outperform direct file reads. Rejecting on grounds of insufficient novelty relative to existing capability, no empirical evidence, and weak community signal.
evaluation.action: ARCHIVE — no integration. The L0/L1/L2 retrieval protocol description is the one extractable technique worth noting if context efficiency becomes a documented gap; flag that possibility in the rejection note rather than integrating now.
